video.title: Why Your Forehand Sprays, and How to Fix It

classification.reason: The coach provides executable drills and instructions, specifically telling the player to nestle the skinny part of the handle into the V of the hand and hit with an open palm to innervate the top haptic reference.

problem.title_as_question: Why does your forehand spray, and how can you fix it?
problem.definition: The forehand sprays and lacks racket face control because the handle size or shape prevents flush haptic contact with the V of the hand, breaking the sensory link needed for timing and face awareness.
prerequisites: semi-western or western style forehand grip

symptoms.description: Forehand shots spray and miss targets inconsistently due to timing and alignment errors in the hitting zone.
Inability to perceive the racket's momentum and pressure profile during loading and release.
Difficulty feeding or self-dropping the ball accurately out of the hand with the forehand grip.

causes.statement: The racket handle is too large or has too wide a top face, preventing the contours of the hand from nestling flush against it.
A broken sensory link deprives the brain's motor program of the high-fidelity haptic feedback needed to self-organize timing.
The top haptic reference is disconnected, leaving the player unable to perceive the pressure profile, racket load, or release point.

angles.summary: Handle geometry and bevel width dictate whether the hand can maintain flush contact during the swing.
Haptic feedback flush against the hand allows the brain to immediately auto-correct timing and contact zone.
Deliberately creating a gap at the top reference ruins racket face control and spray consistency.
Alcaraz's grip style naturally self-organizes into a bigger swing loop when the handle fits properly.

solutions.summary: Check if the handle is crashing into the fingers or getting stuck instead of nestling flush into the contours of the hand.
Nestle the skinny part of the handle into the V of the hand with full contact and hit balls with an open palm.
solutions.external_goal: Direct the ball onto the red target using only the top reference

solutions.summary: Perform roughly a thousand open-palm swings over a month to force the brain to innervate the top of the racket handle.
Test whether you can easily self-drop feed out of your hand and rally using the open-palm forehand grip.
solutions.external_goal: Self-drop feed accurately with the forehand grip

solutions.summary: Place the bottom fingers back onto the handle after mastering the open-palm rally, preserving the exact same momentum perception.
